note: Validation cases that do not meet their expected range. The regression test (crates/sim/tests/validate.rs) tolerates exactly these so that a new failure is caught; they stay failed evidence checks in every assessment. A case is reviewed only when `relevance` states what the deviation means for the intended comparisons, `followUp` names the repair or the limit on use, and `reviewed` is true. Reviewed in calibration round 28 (2026-11-15) on the simulator with physical junction recovery; reasons restate the notes of data/calibration/validation.md.

deviations.reason: Start-up lost time is 0.28 s against 1 to 3 s [FHWA-STM2008]: the simulator has no response delay at the onset of green (about 2 s short).
deviations.relevance: Saturation flow (a1, a2, a4) and signal capacity (b1 to b12) pass, so the missing delay costs about 1.5 s of green per phase that the simulator does not lose: signal capacity is a few percent high at the arterial signals. That favors the arterials slightly against the side streets, so it cannot explain side-street through cars above the counted ranges.
deviations.followUp: Limit on use: signal capacities can be a few percent high. Repair would be a reaction delay at the onset of green in the car-following start, with a cited value.

deviations.reason: Two-way stop minor-right capacity at major 600 per direction is 364 veh/h against 378 to 631 [Brilon1999] (gap formula 505, critical gap 6.2 s, follow-up 3.3 s).
deviations.relevance: Side streets of the study area leave by a right turn onto Alcatraz Ave and Claremont Ave, whose modeled PM flows are about 400 to 500 veh/h per direction. The deviation (4% below the range at 600) makes those exits slightly slower than the gap-acceptance range, which works against side-street routes, so it does not inflate the through-car figures.
deviations.followUp: Limit on use: minor-street right turns onto busy streets are slightly underserved. Repair needs a review of the right-turn gap rule against [Brilon1999].

deviations.reason: Two-way stop minor-right capacity at major 1000 per direction is 172 veh/h against 223 to 372 [Brilon1999] (gap formula 298).
deviations.relevance: Only Telegraph Ave carries about 1,000 veh/h per direction near the study area, and side-street right turns onto it are few. Same direction of bias as e2.

deviations.reason: Signal lane with 300 cyclists/h sharing it keeps 0.63 of its capacity against a floor of 0.70; the range has source ASSUMPTION (no verified HCM bicycle factor, the floor is a guess).
deviations.relevance: The floor is not a published value, and 300 cyclists an hour sharing one lane is far above the cyclist flows of the study area's signalized approaches. It does not bear on the through-car figures.
deviations.followUp: Limit on use: no claim about signal capacity under heavy shared-lane cycling. Needs a verified bicycle adjustment before the range can judge it.

deviations.reason: All-way stop with 300 pedestrians/h on each crosswalk keeps 0.49 of its capacity against a floor of 0.60; the range has source ASSUMPTION.
deviations.relevance: The floor is not a published value. The study area's all-way stops (on Hillegass Ave, Colby St and the cross streets) are residential; crosswalk volumes near 300 an hour there are not expected, though the modeled crosswalk volumes were not checked in this round. If they were that high, the stops would slow side-street traffic, which works against cut-through routes.
deviations.followUp: Limit on use: no claim about all-way stops with heavy pedestrian volumes. Needs a verified pedestrian adjustment.

deviations.reason: All-way stop with 600 pedestrians/h on each crosswalk keeps 0.23 of its capacity against a floor of 0.60; the range has source ASSUMPTION.
All-way stop with 300 cyclists/h per approach keeps 0.60 of its capacity against a floor of 0.70; the range has source ASSUMPTION.
deviations.relevance: As j6: the floor is a guess and the cyclist flow is far above the study area's.

deviations.reason: New in round 32. Two-lane signal approach with 20% left turns, a 3-vehicle pocket that overflows every cycle and 500 veh/h per opposing lane: 792 veh/h per lane against 851 to 1,064, the b9 bound at 20% left, which applies the gap formula of [Brilon1999] with tc 4.1 s and tf 2.2 s to the hourly opposing flow. Round 33: the permitted-left method of [Fambro1991] (left turns only once the opposing queue has cleared, then gaps, then sneakers) puts the left-limited approach at 385 to 706 per lane, so the simulator's 792 is above that method, not below it; with the queue-first left-turn model (`Config::queue_first_left`, off by default) it is 658. Through drivers move around a waiting left-turner (lane changes along a link), and a left-turner that does not fit in the pocket waits at the stop line of the inner lane and turns from there.
deviations.relevance: Not reviewed: left to the project lead. The range and the cited permitted-left method disagree; the expected range needs the lead's review before this case can say whether two-lane approaches with heavy permissive left turns are too slow or too fast.
deviations.followUp: Pending review. Candidate repairs: an expected range from the [Fambro1991] method for this geometry, pocket length from map or field data instead of the 3-vehicle ASSUMPTION, and a left-turner that waits at the pocket entrance instead of turning from the through lane beside a full pocket.

deviations.reason: New in round 33. Permissive left from a left-only lane against 400 veh/h of opposing flow: 402 left turns an hour against 157 to 303 by the permitted-left method of [Fambro1991] (left turns only after the opposing queue clears, Drew's gap model with critical gap 4.5 to 5.1 s and turning headway 2.24 to 2.57 s, 0.88 to 2 sneakers a cycle). A left-turner counts a car starting from the green line as about 4 to 6 s away and takes that gap, and after the 45 s courtesy wait (which runs through the red) it goes ahead of the standing opposing queue; the opposing approach then carries less than it is offered. The queue-first model (`Config::queue_first_left`) gives 246, inside the range, but made the Rockridge PM peak less stable and was not switched on.
deviations.relevance: Not reviewed: left to the project lead. Permissive left turns against moderate and heavy opposing flow are served up to twice as fast as the method allows, and the opposing through traffic correspondingly slower.
deviations.followUp: Pending review. Repair: switch on the queue-first model once protected phases where the field has them (left-turn arrows) are in the network, so that the arterials do not lose capacity they have in reality.

deviations.reason: New in round 33. As p2 with 600 veh/h opposing: 369 left turns an hour against 32 to 167 [Fambro1991]; the queue-first model gives 120.

New in round 33. A one-lane, all-left approach in a phase of its own (protected, phasing observed without timing) discharges 450 veh/h at a green share of 0.30, about 1,500 an hour of green, against s x green share with s 1,500 to 2,000 [FHWA-SIG2004]: 2 veh/h below the lower bound. Single-lane left turns slow to the 5 m/s turn speed (ASSUMPTION); seeds 2 to 5 give 456 to 486.
deviations.relevance: Not reviewed: left to the project lead. Protected left turns discharge at the low end of the observed saturation flows.
deviations.followUp: Pending review. Repair: a cited turn speed or left-turn saturation adjustment.

deviations.reason: New in round 38. A gate feeding a 3-lane link that forks into two branches with lanes of their own passes 0.43 of the free branch's flow while the other branch is queued back to the gate (offered 3,000 veh/h into a lane drop), measured against the same network with the other branch unqueued. Waiting trips leave a gate in order per first link, so trips for the free branch wait behind trips for the queued one. On the network this holds trips for the 52nd St off-ramp behind those for the Martin Luther King Jr Way off-ramp at the SR-24 mainline gate.
deviations.relevance: Not reviewed: left to the project lead. A tested fix (a waiting trip waits only behind trips for the same fork branch) gives 0.64 and leaves every other case unchanged. On PM seeds 1 to 20 it cuts the trips waiting at the SR-24 gate from 143 to 84 and 68 per seed, but the fitted stations do not improve, and it changes the simulator fingerprint. So it was not landed.
deviations.followUp: Pending review. Repair: per-branch waiting at gates (the round-38 patch), together with the lane drop on the Martin Luther King Jr Way off-ramp (case i5).
